title: First Millimeter Flares Detected from ϵ Eridani with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array
question: Search archival ALMA 12-m and ACA observations of the Sun-like star epsilon Eridani for millimeter flaring emission and characterize its temporal, spectral, and polarization properties, as well as constraints on inner dust belt emission.

what.value: Millimeter flare properties for AU Mic and Proxima Centauri

evidence.quote: Previous detection of flares at millimeter wavelengths have mostly come from M dwarfs (see Table 1) (cite: MacGregor:2018a; MacGregor:2020)
Table 1 lists these values in comparison to all other millimeter flares previously detected with ALMA.

evidence.loc: Constraints on Dust Emission from an Inner Debris Disk
evidence.quote: The effective temperature of $\epsilon$ Eridani is $5039\pm126$ K (cite: Baines:2012)

evidence.loc: Constraints on Dust Emission from an Inner Debris Disk
evidence.quote: which implies a photospheric flux at 1.3 mm of $0.53$ mJy (cite: Backman:2009).

what.value: Predicted flux at 1.3 mm of ~0.2-0.3 mJy from extrapolated SED fits for the inner dust ring

evidence.loc: Constraints on Dust Emission from an Inner Debris Disk
evidence.quote: Extrapolating the SED fits for the inner dust ring from (cite: Su:2017) yields a predicted flux at 1.3 mm of $\sim0.2-0.3$ mJy, strikingly consistent with what we determine here.

recipe.goal: Continuum imaging and combined visibility fitting
recipe.method: Create natural weight primary-beam-corrected continuum images using tclean, calculate rms across ten source-free regions, and fit point source models to the combined visibilities using uvmodelfit.
key_parameters: ten source-free regions for rms calculation
assumptions: Point source model at the stellar position

recipe.goal: Create light curves and identify millimeter flares
recipe.method: Run an automatic pipeline using CASA uvmodelfit to fit point source models to each telescope integration step-by-step in time, flagging flux densities above 3 sigma, and confirm candidates by fitting lower and upper sidebands independently.
assumptions: Point source model for the star

recipe.goal: Characterize flare temporal structure, spectral index, and linear polarization
recipe.method: Fit Gaussian functions to flare light curves to measure FWHM (t_1/2), fit point source models with uvmodelfit to upper and lower sidebands independently for spectral index, and fit XX and YY polarizations independently to compute Stokes Q and I for fractional linear polarization |Q/I| at flare peak.
key_parameters: upper (230 + 232 GHz) and lower (219 + 217 GHz) sidebands
ALMA XX and YY polarizations at flare peak
assumptions: Gaussian temporal profile and power-law spectral dependence F_nu \propto \nu^\alpha

recipe.goal: Estimate magnetic field strength in the flare-emitting region
recipe.method: Associate the observing frequency with harmonic numbers s (between 10 and 100) of the electron gyrofrequency \nu_B = 2.83 x 10^6 B(G).

recipe.goal: Measure quiescent stellar and inner dust excess flux density
recipe.method: Fit a point source model using CASA uvmodelfit over all available ALMA observations excluding the flare intervals (E1, E2, E3), and subtract the expected photospheric flux at 1.3 mm.
key_parameters: Exclude flaring intervals E1, E2, and E3
assumptions: Expected stellar photospheric flux at 1.3 mm is 0.53 mJy

score_reason: Archival ALMA project codes are clearly stated and the core method (CASA uvmodelfit per integration on upper/lower sidebands and XX/YY polarizations) is conceptually simple, but the custom pipeline scripts, exact stellar position fixing in uvmodelfit, off-axis primary beam correction in visibility space, and exact time windows for E2/E3 are not specified.
rediscovery_reason: Both ALMA datasets (2013.1.00645.S and 2016.1.00803.S) are public in the archive, the core analysis relies on standard CASA tasks (tclean, uvmodelfit), and the main results are concrete numeric values (flare peak fluxes, durations, spectral indices, polarization limits, and quiescent stellar flux).
